reflections.summary: Won because Corviknight’s Choice Scarf Iron Head swept after Trick Room expired, outspeeding and KOing Farigiraf while capitalizing on Gardevoir-Mega’s missed Focus Blast; however it was fragile—Medicham-Mega, Aegislash, and Archaludon all fell, leaving Corviknight alone at critical HP. The preview was poor: Medicham-Mega was sent into an Armor-Tail/ Fairy-Psychic core where Fake Out is blocked and it is weak to coverage, and no backup reserves were kept to support the locked sweeper.
reflections.adjustment: In the next preview, drop Medicham-Mega (replace with a Fairy-resistant, non-priority breaker) and do not Mega-evolve into this opponent’s Psychic/Fairy core; pair Corviknight with an actual pivot/reserve so Choice-lock never strands it solo; and bring explicit anti-TR or post-TR speed control instead of relying on one sweeper.
reflections.notebook: Durable opponent tendencies: TR duo Farigiraf (Mental Herb, Armor Tail, Relaxed; TR/Psychic/Helping Hand/Protect) + Hatterene (Magic Bounce, Life Orb, Quiet; TR/Psychic/Dazzling Gleam/Protect); offense from Gardevoir-Mega (Timid, Gardevoirite) and Hisui-Arcanine (Intimidate, Focus Sash, Adamant); pool also holds Kingambit (Defiant, Black Glasses) and Milotic (Competitive, Leftovers). Revealed strategic facts: Armor Tail nullifies priority (Medicham Fake Out useless); Magic Bounce reflects status/hazards; Mental Herb cures disruption; opponent will set TR. Future plans: never bring Medicham-Mega into this matchup; avoid leaving Corviknight as the only living reserve without switch-in support; anticipate TR and either block it or guarantee outspeed after it ends; choose any Mega holder that is not weak to opponent’s Fairy/Psychic coverage.

reflections.summary: The game was lost primarily due to Gardevoir's Focus Blast missing Corviknight on turn 7, which would have likely secured a KO. This left Farigiraf in a losing endgame where resisted Psychics couldn't outpace Corviknight's Iron Head, especially with Trick Room expiring. The team composition, with two Psychic/Fairy types and no reliable Steel coverage after Arcanine fell, was poorly suited to the opponent's Steel-heavy team.
reflections.adjustment: For the next game, avoid bringing both Hatterene and Gardevoir-Mega against a team with multiple Steel types. Instead, bring a dedicated Steel counter with reliable moves, and preserve it for key threats like Corviknight. Consider using a different lead that doesn't rely on risky Focus Blast.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's revealed sets: Corviknight (Choice Scarf, Mirror Armor, Jolly, Iron Head, Brave Bird, U-Turn, Roost), Aegislash (Focus Sash, Calm, King's Shield, Shadow Ball, Flash Cannon, Close Combat), Medicham-Mega (Jolly, Fake Out, Close Combat, Ice Punch, Shadow Ball), Archaludon (Bold, Leftovers, Protect, Flash Cannon, Dragon Pulse, Light Screen). Pelipper and Stunfisk held Damp Rock and Shuca Berry but were not used in Game 3. Our team is weak to Steel types; avoid stacking Psychic/Fairy attackers. Need reliable Fire- or Ground-type coverage. Preserve such counters for Corviknight. Trick Room endgame vs Scarf Corviknight is unfavorable if we cannot KO it before TR expires.
